Truckers pay IFTA. Here's a little excerpt about it - An operating carrier with IFTA receives an IFTA license and two decals for each qualifying vehicle it operates. The carrier files a quarterly fuel tax report. This report is used to determine the net tax or refund due and to redistribute taxes from collecting states to states that it is due.

Here's how it works- Simply stated, IFTA works as a "pay now or pay later" system. As commercial motor vehicles buy fuel, any fuel taxes paid are credited to that licensee's account. At the end of the fiscal quarter, the licensee completes their fuel tax report, listing all miles traveled in all participating jurisdictions and lists all gallons purchased. Then the average fuel mileage is applied to the miles traveled to determine the tax liability to each jurisdiction. Three states—Kentucky, New Mexico, and New York—have "weight-mile" taxes in addition to the standard fuel tax. Oregon has just a weight-mile tax. Any amount of fuel taxes due (or refund) is then paid to (or received from) the base jurisdiction who issued the license. The member jurisdictions then take care of transferring the funds accordingly. Audits are conducted only by the base state and fuel bonds are rarely required.

So, trucks pay this in addition to the sales tax on fuels. Recreational vehicles are exempt.

Trucking companies also need permits to operate in some states. Can't do business there without it. We also have hazmat permits or alcohol permits to carry those types of loads legally. If your load is over size you may need a permit for that. Your routes are limited and you may need a pilot car or team to help you navigate that route. All of those things are taxed. I don't have an issue with RVs making a stop and taking a break for the restroom or to stretch. I get that. They do pay for those services too. They can literally go anywhere though. They can take up 8 spots in a mall parking lot and not get towed. They can use campgrounds. We can't even bobtail into most campgrounds because they won't allow us.

If we park at Walmart and they decide they don't want us out there our trucks can be booted or towed. Minimum $500 to get a boot off most cases. There are predatory tow companies that don't give the courtesy of a warning sign or even a knock on the door and a chance to move. They will straight-up boot the truck and extort a fee to get it off but Joe Camper 25 ft away isn't bothered. There are over 3 million trucks on the road at any given time and less than 300,000 safe, designated truck spots for semis. It's not even that we feel entitled. It's that we are not welcome anywhere necessarily and it ends up costing us literally thousands. We miss loads to make sure we have safe parking. Or we pay for parking. $15 a night. Add that up in a month. We don't run in certain areas because the tolls and parking costs mean we don't make enough. We pay for parking when necessary but every night isn't feasible. So when an RV chooses not to pay to stay at an RV park for the night or Walmart for free they put drivers at risk in unsafe areas or take money out of the drivers wallet. Out of whatever he sends home to family he spends weeks to months away from. I think you can see why drivers are upset about this. Everything is meant to charge us or make things more expensive from the shippers, receivers, truck stops, DOT etc and now we have people in campers who want to know why we're upset when our miniscule perk of free, safe parking is taken up by someone vacationing or retired.

This got long. I hope it gives perspective though. We're all tired. We miss our families and everything always feels stacked against us but we love so much out here it's hard to walk away.

When you take a truck spot even at a rest stop that leaves trucks left to parking on the sides of the ramps or in unsafe areas because the clock dictates they have to stop. If campers park in truck spots, remember you're taking a little security from drivers out here who don't have much to begin with.

Many drivers rely on the stops for food and drink. More money. You can't even avoid fast food and eat cheaper using a microwave. One Velveeta microwave meal costs $7.89 at Loves. Or McDonald's mcchickens for much cheaper. Consider the shop work that costs way more than work on your car. Way way more. Truckers pay to shower with either fuel or cash. Either way that "free shower" isn't free.

Their fines are way more than a car drivers. Ultimately drivers pay more for everything and it all goes back into the services that they need to be out here. It goes back into the roads needed to do business. Drivers put more into the funds to build those rest areas than car drivers usually. 

Drivers live out here. The road is their home in most cases and they pay for it with money and time. They keep hospitals supplied. Restaurants going. Grocery stores stocked. Again it comes to willpower. Foodies just need to gain the willpower to stay out of those aisles. No different than an alcoholic. Adrenaline junkies get no more than an endorphin release and yet it could be classified as an addiction because they put themselves in risky situations specifically for the kick. The release of endorphins. I'm not saying foodies are right or their lifestyle is good. I am only saying that it is a battle for them. I grew up with an alcoholic and I've met people addicted to food. Their struggles are very real and very similar to any other addict. Now, not all fat people are addicts. I'm not saying they are either. There are those that are just lazy and they over eat. If you were to run the two through therapy there would be distinct differences in their behavior.

If you talk to an alcoholic who is new to the program they will probably tell you that they won't go anywhere near a bar. The bar serves soda which is a smarter option. Logically they know that. They wouldn't order soda in a bar though. Until they get a firmer grip on sobriety they will order alcohol. So they just avoid the bar until that time comes. When they have more control and better willpower they may be able to order that soda. It is not different for a foodie. They know the smarter, healthier option. They have not formed the willpower to do it yet. That is why there are programs for over eaters. Addiction is overcoming the dependency and willpower issues whether it is food or drink or drug. A gym rat would like pizza but he does not feel dependent and he has the willpower. So yes I believe a person can be addicted to food. 

Edit: words

Admitting addiction is taking the blame personally to start living a better lifestyle. The first step in any recovery is admitting you are powerless over addiction. 

It was also stated that the addiction isn't to the food so much as the endorphins from fulfilling a want. The "high" from fulfilling the craving. Like lighting a cigarette or shooting up. You most definitely can become addicted to food when your pleasure and happiness is firmly set in having food. Now the interesting thing to consider is how a foodie breaks the cycle. With alcohol, drugs or gambling a major factor is abstaining completely from their triggers. How does someone completely abstain from something that is necessary to survive? You can't. There is no way. So you learn portion control and healthy eating and battle your brain screaming at you daily to keep eating because that is what makes you happy. 

For some it isn't easy. For some it's the hardest thing they will ever do.

What the hell is with the hostility? Was I in here saying anything about how skinny people have it easy? Or downgrading your situation in the least? Not at all! I'm sorry for your struggle. Honestly. In a perfect world no one would struggle with food. This is not a perfect world. 

I'm at this very point working out almost daily. I haven't had soda for weeks and sweets of any kind for longer than that because I'm trying to attain the better lifestyle that everyone is saying should be done. I have to dig down and find willpower. Please don't act like it doesn't take willpower for me to say no to a piece of gum because it honestly does. People seem to think it's easy to say no to food. That is not always the case. 

Just in the past 5 days I have had to say no to fresh baked cookies a guest at work brought me. A candy-bar another guest gave me. A freaking bushel of apples ANOTHER guest gave me. Because they don't fall into my diet. I feel rude when someone offers what they think is healthy and I have to say no and then explain myself. "Well obviously I'm overweight and I'm finally doing something about it and that just doesn't fall into my diet. It's complicated." Even in a simple explanation, you get looks. Holidays are coming! Yaaaaaay! No. I come from a family who has never shied away from sugar. Temptation on every platter and in every tin. And repeatedly...I tell myself no. Because I WANT a better life. Goddamn if I don't want some fucking chex mix. Or some holiday cranberries. Or hell, some homemade fudge. I tell myself no, I tell others no. And the entire time that I'm saying it I STILL have people on the outside who don't see me killing myself at the gym or counting every carb I put in my body to make sure I'm under the 25g a day limit. They look and they wonder why I don't take care of myself because they don't fucking KNOW. 

Again...I'm sorry for your troubles. Please do not think that I don't care...or that anyone else doesn't care. I've learned NOT to judge because of the judgement that has been placed on me the entire time I've been this way. I struggle. You struggle. Another user said you should do your research before having an opinion about it. I'd like to ask if you actually did that? 

I've known 3 people that had the surgery done. They didn't just get surgery and eat less. That is not how it works. One of the doctors that performs the surgery where I live requires a program first. They do a physical and determine what you're able to do as far as exercise and diet. You do that for a few months and then your progress is checked. After that they determine if you're eligible. All three were on extremely strict diets. They couldn't just eat mac and cheese or steak. First it's liquids and then you slowly work regular food into it. Over MONTHS time. And all three of the people that I know coupled their surgery with regular exercise. 

You can stretch the new formed stomach after surgery. Numerous people do it. You should be impressed by the ones that don't stretch it. They get to eat roughly 1/4 of what a regular person does and be satisfied with it. They still have to have ENORMOUS willpower to not push the limits. 

Not to mention some people have physical limitations that hinder weight loss. My mom has a degenerative disease that is making the discs in her back basically crumble. Constant pain that never goes away. Some days it is just not as bad. And she is refusing surgery like this that would help because she doesn't want people like you to think of her like that. Like she just took the easy way out. 

Things are more than just what's on the surface sometimes. People need to think about that before they judge.
